openai.feedback:
- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: client/src/components/external/SmartViewer/htmlResourceLoader.ts:129
- Finding: Stylesheet requests bypass the shared loader limits. `text()` calls `fetchTextFile` directly, so linked stylesheets and imports do not count toward the 40-file or 20 MB limits, do not use the six-request semaphore, and are not aborted by `dispose()`. Twenty linked stylesheets can start concurrently; the wrapper timeout stops waiting without cancelling those requests.
- Suggestion: Route stylesheet reads through the same counted, cancellable request queue as images and fonts, with shared file and byte budgets.

- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: client/src/components/external/SmartViewer/htmlInlineAssets.ts:75
- Finding: The 30 MB output limit counts only substituted data URIs. Imported stylesheet bodies are inserted without calling `spend()`, and linked stylesheet bodies are likewise uncounted. Twenty linked stylesheets plus twenty imports can exceed the output limit before any images are embedded.
- Suggestion: Budget stylesheet text and replacement overhead as well as data URIs, and enforce a final document-size ceiling before constructing `srcdoc`.

- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: client/src/components/external/SmartViewer/htmlInlineAssets.ts:69
- Finding: Page-wide import deduplication changes CSS cascade behavior. For example, `@import "red.css"; @import "blue.css"; @import "red.css";` should end with red taking precedence, but the final import remains relative and cannot load in the iframe, leaving blue in effect. The diamond test explicitly expects this semantic change.
- Suggestion: Cache fetched stylesheet text while preserving each import occurrence. Detect cycles using the current recursion stack and bound repeated expansion with the shared output budget.

- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: client/src/components/external/SmartViewer/htmlInlineAssets.ts:84
- Finding: Rewriting drops URL fragments. A valid CSS reference such as `url("icons.svg#check")` becomes a data URI without `#check`, so the browser no longer selects the referenced SVG symbol or fragment. Image attributes take the same path and lose fragments too.
- Suggestion: Separate the fragment from the file path, fetch and cache the file without it, then append the fragment to the generated data URI.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The main rendering and access-control paths are implemented, but stylesheet handling bypasses required resource bounds and changes valid CSS behavior.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
The diff is the implementation *plus* the planning/review artifacts from its own review cycle; the substantive code already incorporates the previously-flagged high findings (output budget `spend`, `dispose()` abort, `[^'"<>]` tag regex, lexical-vs-realpath fallback, memoized owner decision, ADS colon check). Reviewing the code itself:

- Category: bug · Severity: medium · File: client/src/components/external/SmartViewer/htmlResourceLoader.ts (~line 117, `text: async (path) => (await fetchTextFile(urlFor(path))).text`) — `text()` is the one loader method that bypasses every bound: no `acquire()` in-flight slot, no `dispose()` check, no abort, and it isn't counted against `maxBytes`. After `dispose()` the orphaned inlining promise chain (inlineLinkedStyles → processCss) still fetches stylesheets to completion, and `inlineLinkedStyles` fires up to 20 concurrent text fetches. The header comment claims text is bounded by the loader's limits; it isn't.
  Suggestion: route `text()` through the same acquire/dispose/timeout machinery as `dataUri` (or at minimum check `disposed` first and register an AbortController).

- Category: edge-case · Severity: medium · File: server/src/core/session-file/asset-access.ts (~line 60, `isBroadFolder`) — on Windows, `path.relative(dir, home)` (and `os.tmpdir()`) returns an *absolute* path when `dir` is on a different drive; `within()` then returns `false` (it rejects absolute rels), so the home-ancestor and tmp checks silently no-op for pages on a non-system drive. The root check still catches bare roots, but e.g. `D:\Users\shared\report.html` gets the full-subtree asset read with no broad-folder check.
  Suggestion: also treat "different drive than home/tmp" folders via an explicit drive-root/depth heuristic, or compare drive letters before relying on `path.relative`.

- Category: bug · Severity: low · File: client/src/components/external/SmartViewer/htmlMarkupScan.ts (~line 48, `maskNonMarkup` style-block recording) — the block `start` is `html.indexOf(">", lt)`, the first `>` after `<style`. A `<style media="(min-width: 100px)">` or `title="a>b"` makes the recorded CSS range start inside the tag's attribute list, so the wrong substring is processed as CSS (and `</style` escaping applied to it). Content-wrongness only, no security impact.
  Suggestion: scan for the tag's real end respecting quotes (reuse the LINK_TAG-style pattern) before recording `start`.

- Category: edge-case · Severity: low · File: client/src/components/external/SmartViewer/htmlInlineStyles.ts + htmlInlineAssets.ts — `claimImport` is page-wide first-come-first-served: the same stylesheet `@import`ed from two *different* linked stylesheets (or `<link>`ed twice, which `inlineLinkedStyles` fetches independently with no dedupe) is inlined only at its first occurrence; the second `@import` survives verbatim and is dead under the CSP (`connect-src 'none'`), so the page silently loses that style. `releaseImport` only helps on fetch failure, not on the duplicate case.
  Suggestion: leave the duplicate as a no-op or emit the cached inlined body again within the output budget; at minimum document it.

- Category: edge-case · Severity: low · File: client/src/components/external/SmartViewer/htmlResourceLoader.ts (~line 100, `fetchAsset`) — when `Content-Length` is absent (chunked responses), the whole blob is buffered before the `maxBytes` check; up to 6×large files transiently held. Low, but a hostile "asset" server isn't the threat model here (the server is ours), so this is memory-hygiene only.
  Suggestion: stream-count bytes while reading and abort past the cap.

Tests: the new unit tests are genuinely behavioral (byte-exactness of untouched srcset candidates, quote-respecting attribute tokenizer, budget cut-off mid-document, dispose semantics with queued waiters, diamond @import fan-out, perf bound on hostile markup) and would fail against a naive implementation. Server tests cover traversal, symlink escape, ADS/spelling, broad folders, and memo semantics including negative-decision non-caching. Spec requirements 1–5 and all stated limits map to named constants that the tests exercise. No regressions visible: `maskNonMarkup` moved but re-exported; `withTimeout`, `ABSOLUTE_HREF`, `attr` remain available; `inlineLinkedStyles` keeps its original signature with an optional 5th parameter; `sessionFileUrl` and `WIN_DEVICE` changes are backward-compatible.

Overall: ship-with-fixes is close, but every remaining defect is low-to-medium hygiene/edge content, the security-critical server rule matches the spec (including the memoization and accepted residual risk), and the earlier high findings are demonstrably fixed in this diff. Approve with the loader `text()` bound and the cross-drive `isBroadFolder` gap as follow-ups.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
